title: Porter Image Definition
description: Declarative definition of a Porter image: source OCI image, base OS, resources, and how it is assembled into a Firecracker-bootable rootfs.

name.description: Short slug, e.g. 'nginx'. Used by 'porter image install <name>'.

type.description: base = OS foundation (kernel + init + guest runtime; no ports/volumes). application = built on top of a base.

arch.description: Architectures this image is built for.

icon.description: URL or asset-relative path to an icon.

kind.description: github-release: prebuilt artifacts from a GitHub repo's releases (e.g. official Firecracker CI microvm images). dockerfile: build from a Dockerfile in this image's directory. compose: build from a compose.yml in this image's directory.

reference.description: For registries: OCI reference WITHOUT tag. For github-release: 'owner/repo'. For dockerfile/compose: path to the build file relative to repo root (e.g. 'images/myapp/Dockerfile').

guestRuntime.description: Inject the Porter guest agent (health hooks, config-drive handling).

defaults.description: RECOMMENDED resources and exposure. Deployment-time config (porter run / instance config) always overrides these — CPU/RAM/disk are not baked into the image.

health.description: Health check command run inside the guest.

tag.description: The common version tag, shared with the upstream image where one exists (e.g. '1.29-alpine'). Same tag anyone using plain Docker/OCI would reference.
